channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Colette Kress becomes Nvidia's interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigns
item.description: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang is out, and the company's chief financial officer Colette Kress is taking over as interim CEO. She'll have to guide the company through an exceptionally challenging time.
item.content:encoded: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang is out, and the company's chief financial officer Colette Kress is taking over as interim CEO. She'll have to guide the company through an exceptionally challenging time.
item.dc:creator: A Martínez

item.title: Nvidia's CEO resigns after alleged spy scandal. What's next for the company?
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with NYU professor emeritus and AI writer Gary Marcus about the fallout of the Nvidia scandal.

item.title: Investigation into what cause deadly Brooklyn building collapse continues
item.description: Investigators are trying to find out what went wrong after an apartment building collapsed into a nearby construction site in Brooklyn, New York, killing at least eight people.

item.title: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
item.description: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle.

item.title: Trump confronts dwindling options to end conflict with Iran
item.description: After President Trump's midterm election losses and Israel's ongoing political shakeup, Gulf countries are stuck in limbo as Trump's options to end the war in Iran dwindle.

item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Andrew Couts of WIRED about a widespread outage of Microsoft products that has disrupted the life and work of thousands of people.

item.title: Why France -- despite its size -- is losing the trust of the market
item.description: Many rich countries have what have historically been considered very high debt loads. Yet France is being singled out and punished by the markets recently. The reason is credibility.
